gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in a Sun Gold Power set, the SPH6548P's two built-in MPPT inputs cap each panel string at 550 VDC open-circuit, and that the SG48100M 51.2 V battery is sold as talking CAN/RS485/RS232 to SunGoldPower inverters, so the store's own battery and inverter work as one 48 V closed-loop pair.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches in either saved chat (gpt-6, 2026-11-14), so there are no cited or top rival pages to compare against. Its two answers name only generic parts (MPPT controller, LiFePO4, 48 V inverter). They name no model and give no PV voltage limit or battery-to-inverter protocol, and they do not say that one store's inverter, battery and panels are documented to work together. The finding is new but stops short of 3, because the per-string panel count that would decide the array could not be sourced (no maker Voc or temperature coefficient for the panel).
kit_items: Inverter/charger with built-in MPPT: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P, 6.5 kW 48 V split-phase 120/240 V, 2 MPPTs, 550 VDC max PV open-circuit voltage, UL 1741, lithium battery type supported. It is the hub the battery and panels must match.

Battery: Sun Gold Power SG48100M 5.12 kWh 51.2 V 100 Ah wall-mounted LiFePO4 (UL1973), 1 or 2 units. The maker lists CAN/RS485/RS232 and names SunGoldPower among compatible inverters, and its 48 V class matches the SPH6548P's 48 V battery input.

Panels: Sun Gold Power 450 W Monocrystalline PERC (UL 61730, CEC listed), wired in series strings per MPPT so that cold-weather string Voc stays under 550 VDC. The panel count per string is not sourced (see unsourced).
